html:
Nikephoros II Phokas was Byzantine emperor from 963 to 969, and before that the empire's most successful general. He came from the Phokas family, a great military clan of Cappadocia in Anatolia.

As commander he led the expedition that won Crete back from the Arabs in the siege of Chandax in 961, then raided Syria and sacked Aleppo in 962. When Emperor Romanos II died in 963 the army proclaimed Nikephoros, and he married the widowed empress Theophano and ruled as guardian of her young sons, the future Basil II and Constantine VIII.

As emperor he conquered Cilicia, took Cyprus back in 965, and his armies captured Antioch in 969. He backed his friend Athanasios in founding the Great Lavra on Mount Athos. But his heavy taxes for the army, his harsh rule and his austere life made him unpopular in the capital. In December 969 he was murdered in his bedroom by his nephew John Tzimiskes, with Theophano's help, and John took the throne.
sum: Nikephoros II Phokas was Byzantine emperor from 963 to 969, and before that the empire's most successful general. He came from the Phokas family, a great military clan of Cappadocia in Anatolia.
